verdict:
X-band edges did not help. Arm B (arm A fine-tuned with the X-band edge loss) loses to a control fine-tuned the same way without that loss, on held-out Stripmap near and far. SSIM against Lee-filtered Stripmap falls by 0.21 points over all 152 pilot holdout tiles (Wilcoxon p < 0.001). In Houston it falls on 48 of 48 tiles, in Owens (near) by 0.24 (p = 0.003) and in Western Australia (far) by 0.15 (p = 0.014). Arm B recovers slightly more Stripmap edges (0.4 to 1.2 m shorter miss distance) but despeckles less (ENL 166 against 200). At held-out X-band sites its edges sit no closer to X-band edges than arm A's. Under the design's decision rule, X-band leaves training and stays a validation reference only.

Arm A works, mostly as a despeckler. ESRT with the paper's recipe beats bicubic IW on every held-out group: SSIM against Lee-filtered Stripmap rises from 35.2 to 41.7 and PSNR from 21.0 to 22.0 dB. It also beats a Lee-filter-then-bicubic baseline (39.3, 21.7 dB). Most of the gain comes from despeckling (ENL about 190). The 5 m detail it adds correlates only a little better with real Stripmap detail (detail r 0.086 against 0.070 for bicubic), and the outputs are smoother than Stripmap (high-frequency ratio 0.20). Our SSIM and PSNR sit well below the paper's 70.1 and 26.1 dB. We score 3.2 km tiles chosen for structure, on raw and Lee references, while they score whole scenes that are mostly homogeneous fields. The ranking against bicubic agrees with theirs; the absolute numbers do not compare.
data: Stripmap SLCs come from 71 scenes on E: (48 pilot, 13 replacements for Sentinel-1C/1D commissioning acquisitions missing from ASF, and the paper's 10). Madrid had only commissioning scenes, so a Liberia coast cell replaced it. Solomon and Galapagos produced no tiles: the Solomon IW pass misses Rennell Island, and the Galapagos Stripmap footprints lie west of the islands. Fogo's 27 March 2025 scene has no usable IW. Each tile is geocoded with sarsen to 5 m terrain-flattened gamma0, with the EGM2008 geoid added to the Copernicus DEM. Co-registration runs coarse to fine against the same-pass IW RTC VV (10 m NCC, then 5 m phase correlation), and only the IW is resampled. Offsets are pooled per scene: a tile keeps its own offset only if it correlates at r ≥ 0.4 and agrees with its scene within 10 m. That rule drops scenes with fewer than 2 reliable tiles. Water and open ocean (WorldCover) are masked. Splits: Houston, Owens, Western Australia and the paper's three test scenes (read off their Fig. 3) are held out entirely. The paper's two validation scenes and about 15% of tile locations per training region form the validation set.
geoloc:
The first Houston test tile (sm_tiles/test_houston.tif, shown in the earlier quicklook) was upside down. sarsen writes its output south-up (positive y pixel size), and process_slc.py wrote it on a north-up grid without flipping it. Against IW that tile correlated at r = 0.08, and its best match sat 500 to 800 m north or south, which looks like an azimuth timing error. Matching the flipped tile against IW found r = 0.51 at near-zero offset. The fix flips south-up output before multilooking. A second error came from the DEM: sarsen treats DEM heights as ellipsoidal, but GLO-30 heights are EGM2008, so Houston (geoid −28 m) shifted by about 55 m in range. The fix adds the geoid height per tile. The old file is kept as sm_tiles/test_houston_FLIPPED_old.tif, and test_houston.tif is now a correctly processed S1D tile from 2026-10-12.

After both fixes, residual Stripmap-to-IW offsets are small and scene-consistent for every satellite. Median offsets are (−8, +2) m for 17 S1A scenes, (−5, +2) m for 20 S1C scenes and (−16, −1) m for 5 S1D scenes, and the paper's S1A/S1B scenes from 2015 to 2017 sit at 2 to 25 m. Houston's S1A (2023, 2024), S1C (2025, 2026) and S1D (2026) scenes all land at (−16, −1) m, with under 1.5 m spread within a scene. We found no S1C/S1D azimuth timing bias. The cropped-SLC path (cropped_product) geolocates to within these offsets, which rules out a 0.1 s timing error; we did not repeat an uncropped run, which takes over 15 minutes per tile. Timor stands out at about −55 m east in every scene from 2023 to 2026, a stable offset that the co-registration removes. Owens (S6, mountains, low contrast) has the noisiest per-tile offsets (17 to 22 m spread), so its scores carry more registration noise. Two IW passes from Sentinel-1C commissioning (Houston, 2 April 2025, and Fogo) did not line up at all (r < 0.1). repair_iw.py re-paired Houston to an S1A pass from 27 March 2025 (r = 0.51); Fogo had no alternative and was dropped.
arma: Arm A trains three models on 200 training tiles (48 → 96 px patches, histogram-matched Lee-filtered Stripmap target, global 0.1/99.9 percentile min-max, SSIM loss, OneCycleLR max 1e-3, 8,000 steps of batch 16 on a shared RTX 3070). The first is ESRT with the paper's recipe, vendored from Lu et al.'s MIT-licensed code with one input channel. The second is the same ESRT plus our input-consistency term (output average-pooled to 10 m against the IW, L2, weight 0.15). The third is the spike's residual CNN at ×2 with the consistency term. All three land within 0.3 SSIM points of each other, so the consistency term neither helps nor hurts here.
metrics: SSIM and PSNR are computed in the paper's space: [0, 1] min-max dB against the histogram-matched reference, either Lee-filtered (the paper's) or raw. MAE is in dB. Detail r is the correlation of the 5 m detail layer (image minus its 10 m block mean) with Stripmap's, and the HF ratio is its energy relative to Stripmap's. Edge distances use the same Canny detector on prediction and Stripmap (m, capped at 50). ENL, MoI, MoR and Cx are measured on the two most homogeneous 32 × 32 windows per tile, in linear intensity, against the IW input. Stripmap rows show the reference's own ENL and Cx.
stage1:
Stage 1 compares output edges with X-band edges on infrastructure (OSM buildings and roads, or WorldCover built-up). Layover, shadow, slopes over 20°, IW-detected change and water are masked, and every image goes through the same Canny detector. It uses two reference sets. The first is 126 X-band collects more than 150 km from any training tile, paired with IW only (85 have enough infrastructure to score): Capella HH and VV, Umbra and ICEYE. The second is held-out Stripmap tiles that overlap Umbra and ICEYE in Houston and the paper's Tyrol and Franconia scenes. Houston's Capella collects (Baytown) lie outside the Houston Stripmap swath, so Capella enters only through the first set. X-band registers to the IW, never to Stripmap.

The key result is the Stripmap row. Real 5 m C-band Stripmap sits no closer to X-band edges than bicubic IW: 24.1 m against 23.7 m from output edge to X-band edge. It finds more X-band edges (27.9 m against 31.5 m miss distance), but X-band edges are a weak reference for C-band detail at 5 m. Wavelength, look geometry and date differ, and Houston's X-band arrives at different headings and incidences (only 18% of pairs match the Stripmap geometry within 5°). The models improve slightly on bicubic in both directions (about 1 to 2 m) at the sites, consistently across providers. That is consistent with despeckling: fewer spurious edges.
armb: Arm B fine-tunes ESRT arm A for 3,000 steps with the tolerant edge loss. The loss is the share of output edge energy weighted by distance to the nearest X-band edge, free within 5 m and saturating at 20 m, applied on infrastructure only, with layover, shadow, change and water masked and the consistency term kept on. A quarter of each batch is drawn on X-band infrastructure: 173 training pairs (87 ICEYE, 70 Umbra, 16 Capella) from Réunion, Fogo, Mojave, Tahiti, Comoros, Cayman and the paper's German training scene. A control fine-tunes for the same 3,000 steps without the edge loss. Only 15% of training pairs registered to the IW, so the rest rely on the providers' own geolocation; spot checks show them well placed in flat towns, while ICEYE GRD on Réunion's slopes is not terrain-corrected (slopes over 20° are masked). We tuned the edge weight on validation SSIM. 0.05 tied the control (0.4127 against 0.4127) and 0.2 scored 0.4124, so 0.05 is arm B. Paired per-tile tests on held-out data are in the verdict above (full table: armb_paired.txt).
panels: Each model also runs on a 9.6 km IW window around one held-out tile per region (the red box marks the truth tile; the bottom row zooms 1.6 km inside it next to the real Stripmap), and on six landscapes with no Stripmap: Iowa farmland, a Rondônia forest edge, the Swiss Alps, Saharan dunes, Nile Delta villages and Pamplona. All three models despeckle strongly and sharpen roads, field edges and canals. None invents building-scale structure that the IW lacks. ESRT arm A and arm B look nearly the same.
caveats:
• Our tiles are 3.2 km and chosen for structure, so they are harder than the paper's whole scenes. The paper's absolute SSIM and PSNR do not compare with ours; the ranking against bicubic does.
  • Training ran 8,000 steps at batch 16 on a GPU shared with three other experiments, against the paper's 30 epochs at batch 128 over 436k patches. Validation SSIM rose by under 0.005 after step 5,000.
  • There is no change mask between the IW and Stripmap dates (within 6 days): a second IW at the Stripmap date does not exist. Water is masked and the SSIM loss is local.
  • The Lee filter is a classic 7×7 Lee with looks estimated per tile (about 2.5 to 3), close to SNAP's but not identical. Co-registration is a global shift per tile, not Gefolki's dense flow.
  • X-band layover masks use an approximate look azimuth (right-looking, from orbit direction) where the item gives none. Most training X-band pairs did not register to the IW.
  • Owens' registration is the noisiest of the holdouts (17 to 22 m spread within a scene).
